irene: Quick question for the API contract folks — for /v2/generate structured responses, should clients expect optional composite fields (objects/arrays) to be null or omitted? We're seeing some JS SDK callers blow up when they get null instead of an object. Also: some proxies return content-type as `application/json; charset=utf-8`. Do we treat that as equivalent to application/json or enforce exact match?

tom: short answer: treat the charset variant as equivalent. servers should set Content-Type to `application/json` but clients must accept `application/json*` (i.e. any params). for optional composites: prefer omission over explicit null to keep older clients safe.

ashley: +1 on omission. can we add a compatibility note to the schema docs? a lot of third-party json-schema validators treat null vs missing differently.

matt: quick example of the failure mode — we had an SDK that does `resp.metadata.name` and crashes when metadata is null. here's a suggested schema-ish guidance to include in the docs:```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "choices": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object" } },
    "metadata": { "oneOf": [ { "type": "object" }, { "const": null } ] }
  },
  "required": ["choices"]
}
```But my preference is to *avoid* sending `null` for metadata at all — just omit `metadata` if empty.

api-lint-bot: lint:rule:response-nullability -> WARNING: allowing both null and absent for `metadata` increases client parsing complexity. Recommend: deprecate null-for-objects in minor releases; require omission in next major.

tom: implementation note: runtime will normalize responses for hosted API to strip top-level nulls for optional object/array fields when serving stable endpoints. this keeps legacy models that emit nulls covered while steering towards omission. we'll document this in the contract.

ashley: what about streaming/ndjson? some clients parse line-by-line and assume each object has the same keyset. if keys can disappear between chunks, that breaks them.

matt: for streaming we should guarantee presence of keys documented as always-present (required list). optional keys may be omitted on a per-chunk basis. add a note: "clients should guard for missing optional keys when streaming."

irene: decision summary: 1) Treat `application/json; charset=*` as equivalent; update SDKs to accept params. 2) Prefer omission over null for optional object/array fields. 3) Hosted runtime will strip top-level nulls for compatibility. 4) Add linter rule and docs; deprecate null-for-objects in next major. 5) Streaming: required keys guaranteed; optional keys may be omitted per chunk — doc note.

deploy-bot: canary: /api-runtime v2.14.1 deployed to us-west-canary at 2119877600 — response-normalizer enabled.

irene: thanks — I'll open a small PR to add the guidance + the linter rule and add an SDK test that tolerates charset params and absent optional fields. https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/4823 (wip). cc @matt @tom for review.

matt: will review. will add an SDK smoke test to catch the `metadata: null` pattern and ensure we tolerate omission.

ashley: I'll update the doc page and add a streaming note.

irene: perfect. closing this thread once the PR is merged. :thumbsup:
